Subject: Follow-up: procurement path + packaging options (post-demo)

Hi Alex / Samantha 

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align with your procurement team: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary use: multi-tenant customer-facing embeddings + chat for support use cases (spikes during product launches).
- Target latency SLO: 100ms p50 for small text gen, embeddings for search.
- Data residency: US only for now; potential EU in H2.
- Security: SOC 2 + audit logs required; you asked about KMS support.

Procurement questions we discussed can you confirm:
1) Payment method: does Acme prefer PO (net 30) or will your card/virtual card be used for initial purchase?
2) Marketplace: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace (single-contract convenience) or via a direct Redwood quote/PO?
3) Timeline: what is your procurement lead time (e.g., 2–6 weeks)?

Packaging & pricing note (high level):
- Hosted (hosted API): fastest to launch, usage-based billing (on-demand) or committed monthly spend for discounts. Good if you want no infra ops and quick time-to-value.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (monthly/annual commits)  -- predictable unit economics and better sustained throughput for heavy, steady workloads. Often required for predictable budgeting or enterprise SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads needing full network isolation and customer-managed infra + platform fee; typically annual licensing and support.

Common commercial paths for customers like you: start on hosted (card/PO) with a 1–3 month pilot, then move to a committed Dedicated pool if usage grows and you need predictable cost/SLA. If procurement requires a PO and invoice, we can provide a formal quote + SOW. If you prefer AWS Marketplace we can provide a Marketplace listing quote (pricing identical, different contract flow).

I've attached a lightweight pricing spreadsheet and a draft SOW to help your procurement team.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-2026.xlsx (pricing scenarios), SOW-lite.pdf

Next steps:
- Can you confirm procurement preference (PO vs card) and whether Marketplace is preferred?
- Please share point of contact for procurement (name/email) so we can send formal quote + any required reseller paperwork.

Thanks happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps.

Best,

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex and thanks for looping Michael. 

Short answers up front: 
- AWS Marketplace: we are listed and can transact through Marketplace; Rachel (cc) will share the onboarding guide and the exact listing id. Pricing and unit economics are the same; Marketplace just changes invoicing/contract flow.
- PO vs card: we can accept PO (net 30). For pilots that expect to exceed ~$10k/mo, PO is common and will map to either hosted on-demand billing or a short-term committed credit if you want discounted rates.

Commercial options tailored to your procurement rules: 
1) Hosted - PO (on-demand): No commit required; you get standard hosted API billing invoiced monthly. Simple and fastest for procurement.
   - Pros: fast procurement (quote + PO), no infra changes.
   - Cons: higher per-token unit price vs committed pools at scale.

2) Hosted - PO (committed): You sign a short commitment (e.g., $Xk/month for 3 months) in exchange for discounted per-token pricing. Invoiced monthly via PO. Useful if you want budgeting predictability without Dedicated.

3) Dedicated - Reserved capacity (monthly/annual commit): Procurement signs a reservation/commit for a GPU pool; we provide SLA and predictable throughput. Usually requires a longer procurement cycle and an SOW.

4) Private (VPC/on-prem): For next-step conversations if your security team requires network isolation procurement + infra must approve; typically annual contract.

Recommendation given your goals (pilot for embeddings + chat, potential spikes): start on Hosted with a PO (on-demand) for a 4–8 week pilot, optionally convert to a short committed hosted credit if you want immediate discounts. If you expect immediate steady-state high throughput, we can scope Dedicated.

What I'll do now:
- Rachel will share: Marketplace onboarding guide + sample quote id.
- I'll draft a formal quote + short SOW (SOW-lite.pdf attached) for a hosted PO-based pilot and include a committed-option line item so procurement can see both flows.

Michael / procurement: can you confirm the cost center / billing address and whether you need any special invoicing fields (e.g., PO number format)? Also, do you require our W-9 / vendor forms?

If it helps, I'm available Wednesday for a quick 20-min call with procurement to walk the quote.
